Both group names are optional; empty disables the corresponding role.

| Key | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`admin.require_group`](#require_group) | string | `empty` |
| [`admin.soc_group`](#soc_group) | string | `empty` |
| [`admin.auditor_group`](#auditor_group) | string | `empty` |
| [`admin.contact_email`](#contact_email) | string | `empty` |
| [`admin.disabled_message`](#disabled_message) | string | `empty` |

## `require_group`

`string`, default `empty`

The OIDC group a caller must belong to in order to access admin-scoped operations (diagnostics, claims echo, directory sync and probe), plus everything the SOC and auditor roles below can do. Empty disables admin operations entirely. Fails closed: no identity, no group, or no configured group all deny.

```yaml
admin:
  require_group: ""
```

## `soc_group`

`string`, default `empty`

The OIDC group a caller must belong to in order to access SOC-scoped account operations: disabling and re-enabling users and expiring enrollments. Whoever can contain an account can also release it, so a SOC disable of an admin never needs an admin to undo it. SOC is a child role of admin, so `require_group` members hold SOC access regardless of this setting; empty therefore narrows SOC operations to admins rather than disabling them. SOC members also hold auditor access (they need the directory and enrollment lists to find what to contain). Fails closed: no identity, or membership in neither group, denies.

```yaml
admin:
  soc_group: ""
```

## `auditor_group`

`string`, default `empty`

The OIDC group a caller must belong to in order to access auditor-scoped operations (viewing effective configuration, cross-user certificate history). Auditor is a child role of both admin and SOC, so `require_group` and SOCGroup members hold auditor access regardless of this setting; empty therefore narrows auditor operations to those roles rather than disabling them. Fails closed: no identity, or membership in no granting group, denies.

```yaml
admin:
  auditor_group: ""
```

## `contact_email`

`string`, default `empty`

Superseded by branding.support_email, which is the one setting for who to ask about this deployment and is shown on the account-disabled page along with the login page and the footer. It is still read, but only when branding.support_email is unset, so an existing configuration keeps its contact; the server logs a warning at startup while it is the one in use.

```yaml
admin:
  contact_email: ""
```

## `disabled_message`

`string`, default `empty`

Free-text shown on the account-disabled page below the contact email. Useful for explaining why the account was disabled or what the user should do next.

```yaml
admin:
  disabled_message: ""
```
